messages.content: How is the air quality in Los Angeles right now?

function.name: plant_biomass
function.description: Calculate the biomass of a plant species in a given area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, you can quickly find up‑to‑date information from a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to Check |
|--------|--------------|
| **EPA AirNow** | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, select “California” → “Los Angeles County,” and you’ll see the current AQI, pollutant breakdown, and forecast. |
| **AirVisual (IQAir)** | Go to https://www.iqair.com/usa/california/los-angeles and click “Live AQI.” |
| **Weather.com** | Search “Los Angeles AQI” or open the weather app; many apps display the AQI in the main forecast card. |
| **Mobile Apps** | “AQICN,” “Plume Labs: Air Report,” or “EPA AirNow” apps give push notifications for changes. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, just open one of those sites or apps and you’ll see the current AQI value (e.g., 42 = “Good,” 101–150 = “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups,” etc.) along with the dominant pollutant (PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, etc.).
